summary: After the broker drops the socket, nothing of the last connection carries over: the first tk after the reconnect has no feed time, and the frame leaves ltt out rather than pass a receipt time off as one. The next tf with a time brings ltt back, and a partial tf after it keeps that time.

notes: Partial updates overlay within a connection only: docs/port/market-data-frames.md, Partial-update feeds; lead correction 2026-11-09, .lane/107/decisions.md: a field a partial packet omits is unchanged, not unknown. The desktop drops its snapshots on a new connection; the web keeps them (audit appendix item 11), so its first frame after the reconnect carries the feed time from before the outage.
Lead ruling (round 3 review): on a partial-update feed, no trade time yet in this connection means ltt is left out; a receipt time is never passed off as a trade time.

deviations.reason: The web sends AliceBlue's feed time ft as ltt in epoch seconds, an integer since web #2473 (aliceblue_adapter.py `_feed_time`, `_quote_fields`); the docs key ltt is epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md).

After the reconnect the first tk carries no feed time: the web keeps its snapshot across the reconnect and sends the feed time from before the outage as ltt (aliceblue_adapter.py `_update_market_snapshot`); the desktop starts the connection afresh and leaves ltt out until AliceBlue sends one.
